rounds.text: IDFC First Bank is experiencing accelerating earnings growth [E58] with a trailing twelve months compounded profit growth of 77% [E17], which outpaces the sector median profit growth of 25.0% [E65] and satisfies the screen for year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% [E56]. Supporting this bottom-line surge is consistent top-line expansion, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 20% over five years [E12] and 21% over three years [E13]. This momentum has helped push the stock to 90% of its 52-week range [E5] while maintaining a price-to-book ratio of 1.52x [E2]. Conceded: the bank's 3-year compounded profit growth is negative at -13% [E16], its ROA of 0.44% lags the sector benchmark of 1.79% [E8], and its P/E of 32.4x and P/B of 1.54x sit above their respective sector benchmarks of 20.12x [E6] and 1.36x [E7].

IDFC First Bank trades at an exorbitant P/E of 32.1x to 32.4x [E1, E6], representing a massive premium over the sector benchmark of 20.12x [E6]. This lofty multiple is completely disconnected from the bank's actual profitability, evidenced by a dismal Return on Assets (ROA) of just 0.44% compared to a sector benchmark of 1.79% [E8]. Furthermore, the longer-term earnings trajectory reveals severe instability, with compounded profit growth over 3 years contracting by -13% [E16]. The stock is currently priced near perfection, sitting at 90% of its 52-week range [E5], while offering a negligible dividend yield of only 0.29% [E4]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at a robust 77% [E17] and 5-year sales growth is 20% [E12].

While the bear points to a P/E of 32.1x to 32.4x [E1, E6] exceeding the sector benchmark of 20.12x [E6], this premium is fully justified by accelerating earnings growth [E58] and a trailing twelve months compounded profit growth of 77% [E17] that vastly outperforms the sector median profit growth of 25.0% [E65]. Conceded: the bank's ROA of 0.44% is currently below the sector benchmark of 1.79% [E8]; however, this is due to an active capex build-up phase, with CWIP up 52.7% to Rs 113 Cr [E30]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 3 years contracted by -13% [E16], but this short-term volatility is outweighed by a strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 28% [E15] and recent YoY profit growth exceeding 20% [E56]. Finally, sitting at 90% of its 52-week range [E5] reflects robust market confidence supported by 21% compounded sales growth over 3 years [E13], making the low dividend yield of 0.29% [E4] a minor detail for a rapidly expanding business.

While the bull argues that a P/E of 32.1x to 32.4x [E1, E6] is justified by a 77% TTM profit growth rate [E17], this ignores a severe historical compression where 3-year compounded profit growth contracted by -13% [E16]. Conceded: 5-year compounded profit growth sits at a strong 28% [E15]. However, the bull's attempt to excuse the bank's weak 0.44% ROA against a 1.79% sector benchmark [E8] via a 52.7% increase in CWIP to Rs 113 Cr [E30] is unconvincing, as bank capital expenditure on physical work-in-progress does not conventionally explain a massive structural profitability deficit relative to peers. Furthermore, citing robust market confidence from the stock trading at 90% of its 52-week range [E5] clashes with the meager 0.29% dividend yield [E4] and a sluggish 10-year compounded share price growth of just 5% [E18].
